title: What If a City Reversed Its River? Chicago Did in 1900

scenes.text: What if a city made a river flow backward? Chicago did it on purpose.
Waste from the Chicago River flowed into Lake Michigan, the city's source of drinking water.
Cholera and typhoid were the fear. Engineers proposed sending the river toward the Mississippi instead.
On January 2, 1900, the last dam was broken open, and the flow turned around.
Downstream, St. Louis filed an injunction on January 17, but the Supreme Court later ruled for Chicago.
Today the district treats about 1.3 billion gallons of sewage a day, for more than five million people.
